reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the exact pair, reopened the 2026–27 EER Appendix 1b, Article 4.2b and the DNUA course material. Reconstructed the 180 EC example by separating the single longitudinal credit, four rotating modules, and Year 2 profile. Tested each documented preparation dependency against a coherent third-year course order. Revisited the workbook descriptions and topics for the changed alignment and progression, then compared the source findings with the frozen record. This was a same-AI pass.
findings: The September 2026 Dutch full-time Medicine cohort starts DNUA. The EER Appendix 1b credits reconcile to 165 EC of compulsory major and 15 EC of Year 2 profiling. Year 1 is 38.5 EC in core blocks, 9 EC in carousel modules and 12.5 EC in longitudinal courses. Year 2 is 42 EC in core blocks and lines, 3 EC in the remaining carousel module and 15 EC of profiling. Year 3 is 60 EC including 1 EC for the cross-year progress test. Adopted values for Movement and Perception and Lifespan are 10 EC each. The profile courses require intermediate level or above and approval without overlap with compulsory courses.

EER Art. 4.2b requires all Year 1 credits and at least 45 EC from Year 2 including Year 2 clinical reasoning and practical line education before the 2 EC preparation block. The 9 EC workplace course follows the preparation block and hospital induction, adult resuscitation certification and history-taking training. Workplace assessment uses evidence of competence, clinical performance and professional conduct in a portfolio. The 13 EC Science and Bachelor Final Project requires the Year 2 interdisciplinary line. The progress test runs four times per year with attainment requirements towards graduation and carries a single credit. The normal Year 1 study advice threshold is 45 EC and differs from the complete Year 1 requirement for the clinical preparation block.

The preparation block and required clinical skills occur before the 9 EC workplace course. The clinical portfolio is assessed. Neither UCR composition provides this medical progression. The UCR courses provide substantive academic coverage of cellular function, organ physiology, drug action and mental health.

UCR Anatomy covers urinary and reproductive structures and its placement is a bounded subject overlap. Introductory brain and behaviour covers mental disorders as well as nervous-system function. These two alignments leave clear scope for the broader Utrecht components. Psycholinguistics must be in 2027h1 after the brain and behaviour prerequisite. Both 24-course sets remain intact, with the evidence and title versions verified.
